A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDUMATH study and contain readable text, figures, tables, and appendices. The appendix material can be matched despite v2 inserting a pipeline appendix and renumbering subsequent appendices and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original teacher annotations, model evaluations, training ablations, error analyses, and a student study at two elementary schools.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports chance-adjusted agreement statistics for the existing judge-validation sample.

M1.justification: The annotation and filtering pipeline, Gemma 3 12B supervised finetuning and KTO stages, and ModernBERT filtering of the 12B and Qwen 3 30B models remain unchanged. The new pipeline diagram illustrates the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ASDIV/STEM data, dataset comparisons, 38 standards combinations, 188 student-interest topics, and two school-study scenarios covering grades 3–5. The removed NumGLUE citation was not an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.5, Gemma 3 12B/27B, and Qwen 3 30B/235B. The newly cited GPT-5 System Card does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 expands judge-validation metrics from percentage agreement to percentage agreement plus Cohen's kappa. The 100-item validation sample, generation budgets, training splits, prompts, and student-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-stage ablation, topic breakdown, error-type analyses, interest-customization experiment, and worked examples are retained. Added explanations of these analyses do not introduce new ablations, robustness tests, or cases.

E5.justification: v2 adds Cohen's kappa reporting for human-human and human-LLM agreement in Section 4.1. Existing standard deviations, standard errors, and significance reporting remain unchanged; no additional runs or seeds are reported.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports kappa values of 0.34 between human annotators and 0.30 between annotators and Gemma 3 27B IT. All 13 tables retain their numerical results, including EDUMATH MaC rates of 85.9% and 94.6%; the change from 1.3 to 1.30 in Table 2 is equivalent formatting.

T1.justification: The criterion definitions and mathematical descriptions are retained, with no added or revised formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations. The added kappa statistics have no accompanying mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same dataset-novelty, model-performance, and student-study claims. Editorial tightening and softer concluding language do not materially change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for grade restrictions, asymmetric human-LLM filtering, fixed-prompt comparisons, and reuse through standards mapping. It interprets the kappas as fair agreement and adds a positive interpretation linking automatic metrics with MaC, while removing the explicit qualification that EDUMATH 12B questions are slightly harder to read.

D1.justification: v2 removes the ARTE readability-tool attribution, the explicit Prolific screening-criteria detail, and the explanation of why some ASDIV questions required rewriting. Training hardware, hyperparameters, checkpoints, prompt templates, and code/data access statements remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds two Li et al. papers, Tang et al.'s MathScale, and the GPT-5 System Card, while removing NumGLUE and ARTE references. It adds limited comparisons with prior evaluation and filtering practices without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 tightens sentences throughout the main text, adds two authors, changes correspondence formatting, and inserts a pipeline appendix before the existing appendices. The main section sequence and five-phase narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the pipeline diagram as Figure 2, revises Table 2's caption and bold emphasis, and relocates existing figures and tables through reflow. Existing displays are retained, and printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: The added chance-adjusted agreement statistics make the central LLM-judge validation more informative, and Figure 2 clarifies the existing pipeline. These provide modest gains in transparency and clarity, despite the loss of the ARTE attribution and the explicit EDUMATH 12B readability qualification. The experimental scope and headline results remain unchanged.
